title: USA-China Strategic Rivalry
overview: Since 2018, escalating tariffs, export controls, and tech restrictions have driven partial economic decoupling between the US and China. Rather than uniform global fallout, exposure varies sharply by country depending on manufacturing entanglement, export dependence on the US, and whether that country is a 'China+1' relocation destination or remains deeply tied to Chinese supply chains.

title: Russia-Ukraine War (Ongoing)
overview: Beyond the 2022 invasion shock already covered as a historical case study, the ongoing war continues to disrupt global grain/food trade and European energy supply. Russia and Ukraine together supplied over a third of world wheat exports and over half of world sunflower oil pre-war - impact is NOT concentrated near the conflict; geographically distant, food-import-dependent countries have often been hit harder than nearby ones.

title: India-Pakistan Conflict (2025)
overview: A real 87-hour India-Pakistan war occurred in May 2025, the most serious escalation since the 1999 Kargil War. Beyond the two combatants, the clearest third-party exposure is China - simultaneously Pakistan's key ally/investor (the $65B China-Pakistan Economic Corridor) and India's largest trading partner - putting Beijing in a uniquely exposed, conflicted position. Central Asian economies with deep, fast-growing Chinese trade ties face secondary spillover risk.
